acceptance.status_reason: Every clause met. The four routes returned 404 on the pre-release dry run and return 401 now, so the hookup is what moved them, and 401-with-no-identity is the owner gate holding rather than an open surface. INVOCATION NOTE: run from the MAIN tree, not the release worktree. The first attempt from the worktree FAILED for a pure instrument reason -- the check shells out to its sibling `_r2_probe.py`, which lives in the checks directory that the release branch does not contain, so python reported 'can't open file' and the SSM params file was never written (status=NONE, every field empty). That failure is recorded rather than hidden because its output looks like a dead host: every probe field read empty. AC3 is SERVED-scoped -- it grades the live host and reads nothing from HEAD -- so the tree it runs from cannot change its measurement, which is why the main tree is the sound place to run it and the worktree is not.

mutant.description: The governing order names no mutant, so none is owed and none was run. What stands in its place is a NEGATIVE CONTROL on every discriminating read, because an all-equal comparison that cannot fail is not evidence.
mutant.expected: n/a -- the spec names no mutant.
mutant.observed: Three controls fired and all three discriminated. (1) The live-base read: 94 of 94 app files equal d3c31e972e, while the SAME instrument against 1e32562729 read 2 DIFFERENT -- exactly MX-r-9's two shipped files -- so the base was established by content and the mislabelled -latest was not relied on. (2) The post-act running-bytes read: 98 of 98 equal to the release, while the same comparison against the superseded base read 2 changed and 4 new, which is precisely the payload. (3) The cold probe's cache guard: cache_at_start was asserted and printed 0 on all 8 samples, and a non-empty cache would have VOIDED the sample (rc=3) rather than reported a fast one -- row Z-S32's defect, where a warm module-level cache made a second handler in the same process look 21x faster than its own mechanism allows.

determinism.method: The load condition was sampled 8 times at the act (3 + 3 + 1 + 1, one handler per interpreter), and the same remedied bytes had been sampled 12 times about 1.5 hours earlier at a 55x larger population. The tool surface was read twice through one reader. The running-bytes comparison was taken once but over a complete 98-file denominator with a negative control.
determinism.observed: Stable within each population and directional where this cell moved the world. THE ONE THING A READER MUST NOT TAKE AT FACE VALUE is the act-time timing: records_scanned read 85, against 4,543-4,699 in every earlier measurement. That was not left to inference -- the store was counted directly: dt=2026-10-10 held 87 objects against 4,972 in dt=2026-10-09 and 2,250 in dt=2026-10-08, and the newest key was written during the measurement, so the probe reads the right source and the fabric genuinely wrote ~57x fewer activity records today. The bar is therefore claimed MET at BOTH ends of the observed range -- 85 records at 1.087 s here, and 4,699 records at 13.828 s in the AMENDMENT 5 re-measure -- and is NOT extrapolated from a quiet store. One handler moved the WRONG way: gitstate read 10.586 s against 3.854 s yesterday, a 2.7x increase while every activity-store handler got ~19x faster, over a git-history population that grows monotonically and does not drain overnight. It is well inside the bar now and it is the margin that will erode.

compiler_tools.invocation: printf to "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/info/sparse-checkout" then git read-tree -mu HEAD
compiler_tools.result: FAIL then PASS, and the failure is the keeper: `git sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/data/transcripts/'` had its leading-slash pattern rewritten by MSYS to 'C:/Program Files/Git/data/transcripts/'. The re-include silently never applied -- meeting_allowlist.json, which deploy-to-ec2.sh REFUSES without, was simply absent -- while `git sparse-checkout list` cheerfully printed the mangled pattern as if it were in force. Writing the pattern file directly is the fix, and in a linked worktree `.git` is a FILE, so the naive .git/info path fails with 'Not a directory'.
